subject: Glidepath: vendor replacement pricing & carveouts
messages:
From: Caroline Yates <caroline@yates-analytics.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@yates-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Vendor replacement — can Redwood match and provide replacement path?

Hi Priyom,

We're evaluating a move off our current inference vendor and I wanted to get a clear sense of Redwood's playbook for two asks:

1) Price parity / match: they have offered us an effective blended rate after credits that is lower than your list. We need a structured offer (credits, prepay, term) that nets comparable TCO over a 12–18 month horizon.
2) Technical carveouts & glidepath: they guarantee some operational behaviors during cutover (fixed latency SLA, shared KV cache migration assistance, and a 2-week rollback window). We need a proposal that maps to similar operational protections and clear contract carveouts if we miss milestones.

Can you share a simple glidepath (milestones + credits tied to go-live) and any standard carveouts you can offer? Also attach a sample SOW or term summary that procurement can review.

Thanks — happy to set a call next week.

Caroline
Head of Cloud Platform
Yates Analytics

P.S. copying contracts so they can chime in on what procurement needs to see.

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: Caroline Yates <caroline@yates-analytics.com>
Cc: contracts@yates-analytics.com, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor replacement — can Redwood match and provide replacement path?

Caroline — thanks for the note and context. High level response below; attaching a concise glidepath + draft SOW for procurement to review (see attachments).

Quick summary:
- Price approach: we can structure a blended economics package that uses a combination of 6 months of usage credits + a tiered discount on committed monthly spend. For Yates' sized workload (est. 60B tokens/year), that nets to within ~5% of the competitor effective TCO over 12 months.
- Glidepath & carveouts: we propose a three-phase glidepath (pilot, staged cutover, full cutover) with milestone-linked credits and a 14-day operational rollback clause. SLA credits apply if p50 latency exceeds target during the staged cutover.
- Technical support: dedicated onboarding engineer, 2-week dedicated cache-transfer support window, and automated KV export helpers to reduce manual work.

I included a Cost_Comparison_Table.xlsx (simple TCO calc), Glidepath_Term_Summary.pdf (milestones + credits) and a draft SOW. Happy to revise numbers after a short call with your procurement/infra team.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-min alignment call this week to confirm target latency & rollback triggers.
2) Procurement reviews SOW; we iterate legal carve language.

If that works, I can pull Jordan into the thread to lock the concessions cadence and get an internal approval path.

Best,
Priyom Das
Principal Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Glidepath_Term_Summary.pdf (2 pages), SOW_draft.docx, Cost_Comparison_Table.xlsx

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Vendor replacement — Yates (need approval band + concession plan)

Team — forwarding Caroline's ask. Key asks to decide:

1) Credit structure banding: do we do 6 months credits + 3-tiered committed discount (5%/10%/15%) or a steeper upfront credit + smaller committed discount? Caroline's expectation: competitor used ~30% upfront credit + 12-month price lock. She'll push for credits up front.
2) Rollback & carveout language: procurement wants a 14-day rollback window with no penalty if we miss staged cutover SLA. We should define objective rollback triggers (eg. sustained p95 > X ms for 30m or error rate > Y).
3) Legal risk: will we accept a unilateral termination right tied to an SLA during the staged cutover? If so, limit it to a specific monetary cap (eg. credits earned + 1 month of committed spend).

Proposed internal position:
- Offer A (aggressive): 30% onboarding credit (applied month1), 10% committed discount for 12 months, SLA rollback window 14 days with credit cap = 2 months committed spend.
- Offer B (balanced): 6 months of progressively applied credits (10% month1, 8% month2–3, 4% month4–6), 12-month price lock at -8%, rollback window 14 days, credit cap = credits applied.

I need quick sign-off on which band to propose. If Offer A, we should flag for VP approval due to credit size.

Jordan / Lauren: any objections or alternative structures? Also confirm that we can deliver the technical KV export helpers in the SOW timeline.

Thanks — Priyom

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor replacement — Yates (need approval band + concession plan)

Priyom — quick notes from my side:
- I support Offer B as default. It's defensible commercially and easier for finance to model.
- If Caroline pushes hard, we can escalate Offer A but require a 12- or 24-month commit minimum and a non-refundable onboarding milestone payment (covers initial infra warm-up).
- Tech feasibility: engineering can provide KV export helpers and a 2-week dedicated onboarding window. We should put explicit rollback triggers in the SOW to minimize ambiguity (p95 threshold + error-rate floor).

Lauren — can you draft the Offer B numbers (credit schedule + expected monthly committed tiers) and a short internal approval memo? I'll queue this with VP if they ask for Offer A.

Jordan
Director of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: Caroline Yates <caroline@yates-analytics.com>
Cc: contracts@yates-analytics.com, jordan.blake@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor replacement — can Redwood match and provide replacement path?

Caroline — thanks for the patience. Based on internal alignment we've put a concrete balanced proposal together (summary below). Full glidepath + draft SOW attached.

Balanced Proposal (Offer B):
- Economics: 6-month onboarding credit phased (10% month1, 8% months2–3, 4% months4–6). 12-month price lock at -8% on committed monthly spend.
- Commit recommendation: 12-month minimum at agreed committed monthly token band (we propose the middle band based on your estimates; see attachment for tiered outcomes).
- Glidepath: Pilot (2 weeks) -> Staged cutover (up to 30 days) -> Full cutover. Milestone credits released at successful completion of Pilot and Staged cutover.
- Technical protections: dedicated onboarding engineer, KV export helpers, and a 14-day operational rollback window during staged cutover. Rollback triggers: p95 latency > 250ms sustained for 30 minutes OR error rate > 2% sustained for 15 minutes.
- Cap on carveout liability: equal to total credits applied during onboarding period + one month of committed spend. No unilateral termination outside these triggers.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached Glidepath_Term_Summary.pdf and SOW_draft.docx and send procurement's preferred redlines.
2) If acceptable, sign the attached term summary and we'll generate the DocuSign envelope for the SOW.

If you want us to present to procurement directly, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough early next week.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Principal Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
